title: High-density legend compression and color-token audit for time-series charts
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Our current time-series legend and tooltip implementation creates thousands of DOM nodes and uses hard-coded color values that underperform for high-density charts (100+ series) and fail several WCAG contrast checks in dark mode. This causes jank on low-powered machines and prevents screen readers from getting meaningful summaries because the legend is mirrored verbatim into the DOM for every series.

Goal: Replace the per-series DOM-heavy legend with a compressed, accessible representation that preserves discoverability and keyboard navigation, reduces DOM nodes by at least 80% in high-density cases, and consolidates color usage into chart design tokens with clear naming and contrast requirements. Maintain parity for existing keyboard flows and integrate with existing console theming tokens.

Scope: design tokens audit for chart colors, legend compression pattern (collapsed + overflow menu), tooltip content structure and aria-announcement strategy, keyboard-first focus indicators, and performance guidance for engineering (canvas+DOM hybrid approach). Exclusions: deep changes to chart rendering runtime (ENG to scope) and embeddable panel orchestration for now.

Why now: Growing support tickets and performance telemetry (see attachments) show frequent slowdowns when users open dashboards with 60-300 series. This is prioritized for the upcoming console release to improve perceived performance and accessibility compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Legend renders a compressed summary for >12 series with a single semantic list item per visible group and an accessible overflow menu for the rest.
Interactive hover/focus still reveals series-specific tooltip content, but tooltip DOM is created on demand and re-used (single tooltip container).
Contrast audit completed: all chart color tokens meet 4.5:1 against background in both light and dark themes (or have explicit assistive labels).
Keyboard navigation: Tab reaches legend, Arrow keys traverse visible items, 'M' toggles overflow menu; screen readers receive a concise aria-live summary when legend focus changes.
Performance: DOM node count for legends reduced by >=80% in pages with 100 series; first interaction latency on low-end machines improves by at least 30% (benchmarks attached).
Design tokens added/renamed and documented in the token spec with migration notes for engineers and a deprecation plan for old tokens.
design_notes:
Proposed patterns: 1) Compressed legend row shows up to 8 visible series (configurable). Each visible item shows a 10px color swatch (CSS-based) and a truncated label. 2) Overflow is a single button "+N" that opens a keyboard-accessible menu with virtualized list items. 3) Tooltip container should be singletons: create on first hover/focus and reuse to avoid repeated DOM churn. 4) For screen readers, do not replicate every series into the DOM; instead expose a summarized aria-live region ("Showing 24 series; focus to explore"). 5) Provide an opt-in prop for engineering to force full legend for smaller datasets or admin debugging.

Token guidance: introduce semantic tokens named chart.series.X, chart.swatch.border, chart.background.overlay, chart.accessible-label-contrast; avoid color tokens like "blue-500" inside chart components. Document fallback palette for quantized/low-color modes and a high-contrast override for accessibility testing.
decisions: Use hybrid rendering: canvas for series shapes + minimal DOM for interactive controls to minimize reflow.
Keep a single tooltip DOM node reused across hover events rather than per-series tooltips to reduce memory pressure.
Prefer semantic tokens over direct palette references to enable themeable contrast tuning without code churn.
Collapse legend into a summarized DOM structure for datasets >12 series; provide a virtualized overflow menu for full list access.
Announce summaries to assistive tech via aria-live instead of creating 100s of offscreen DOM labels.
